solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prime minister aboard HMS India upset sailor

indicators.note: a passenger aboard a vessel is inside it, so one piece sits within the other
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken letter by letter as the fodder
PM is the standard abbreviation for Prime Minister

explanation.surface: The premier boards a Royal Navy ship called India, which upsets one of the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset sailor' looks like a person who is distressed, but 'upset' works backwards on the ship's name, and the premier then boards the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A midshipman is a junior naval officer rank, historically a boy trainee, so he is a kind of seaman.

clue.text: Something put on road island — a tree

parts.note: macadam is the crushed-stone surfacing laid on roads
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Roadworks: something is laid on a road on an island, and a tree is there too.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'a tree' look like a single item, but the 'a' belongs to the wordplay and only 'tree' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The macadamia is an Australian evergreen that bears edible round nuts, so it is a species of tree.

clue.text: Lament mind-set developing destructive action

indicators.note: something developing is changing its form, so the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone bemoans a negative attitude that is growing into something destructive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lament' reads as a verb, but both it and 'mind-set' are just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismantlement is the taking apart or demolition of something, an act that destroys what was built.

clue.text: One who succeeds is regularly cheerier

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A successful person is, predictably, more cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeds' suggests doing well, but here it means following someone into a title or estate.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the person who inherits, taking over the position or property after its holder dies.

clue.text: Set on distant objects, girl cycles

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing set on another stands above it, fixing the order of the parts

explanation.surface: A girl fixes her gaze on faraway things, or goes round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl is written last but goes first: in a down answer she is set on top of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny-farthings are Victorian bicycles with one huge front wheel and a tiny rear one, so they are cycles.

clue.text: Intention to avoid November when climbing mountain

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top
to avoid something is to keep it out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A plan to skip the month of November when going mountaineering.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAN without its N leaves PLA, which climbs up the grid as ALP.
explanation.definitionFit: An alp is a high peak, the word taken from the Alps range of central Europe.

clue.text: What tailors use to record sizes?

parts.note: to tape something is to record it

explanation.surface: A question about the tools a tailor uses for noting customers' sizes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one description, but it splits into a definition and a two-part charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailors take body measurements with flexible marked strips, and these tape measures are their basic instrument.

clue.text: Gelatinous substance got from a fish

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A jelly-like substance extracted from a fish, as gelatine sometimes is.
explanation.walkthrough: The gar, or garfish, is a crossword favourite for a short fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly extracted from seaweed, used to set foods and to grow bacteria in laboratory dishes.

clue.text: Eastern father keeping one of Plato's works in desk

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: the Crito is one of Plato's dialogues, set in Socrates' prison cell

explanation.surface: An oriental patriarch keeps a volume of Plato in his desk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crito is a short dialogue about Socrates refusing to escape prison; the father holds it just after his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An escritoire is a writing desk with drawers and a hinged flap, a French word for this piece of furniture.

clue.text: Arranged a Pisces maiden's fantasy?

indicators.note: things arranged are put in a chosen order, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: M is a maiden over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A young woman born under Pisces has arranged her dream life.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, recorded as M on the scoresheet.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapism is retreat into imaginary pleasures to get away from reality, which is what fantasy offers.

clue.text: Dazzling, like a mirror cat's reflected in

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run the other way

explanation.surface: A cat catches sight of itself in a dazzling mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the cat is reflected, giving TAC, and placed in SPECULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spectacular is strikingly impressive to look at, the way a brilliant display dazzles the eye.

clue.text: Not clear cut how hunger gets resolved

indicators.note: something resolved is broken down and worked out afresh, so the letters are recast

explanation.surface: It is unclear how a famine will be brought to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not clear cut' reads as 'uncertain', but it means literally not cut cleanly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough-hewn timber or stone is shaped coarsely without smoothing, so its edges are far from neatly finished.

clue.text: Meat cut up for person

indicators.note: in a down entry up means read from bottom to top
cutting something short removes its tail, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: Meat is chopped up to feed someone.
explanation.walkthrough: FLESH loses its last letter to become FLES, which reads upward as SELF.
explanation.definitionFit: One's self is one's own individual identity, so the word can stand for a particular human being.

clue.text: File with contents of folk's foolish nonsense

parts.note: a folder is a file for papers

indicators.note: the contents of something are what lies inside, so only its inner letters are kept

parts.note: the inside of the word, without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dossier full of people's silly talk.
explanation.walkthrough: FOLDER plus the inside of fOLk gives FOLDEROL.
explanation.definitionFit: Folderol means trivial or foolish talk or fuss, originally a meaningless refrain in old songs.

clue.text: Formal surrender parade — not professional

indicators.note: not having something means it is absent, so those letters are removed

explanation.surface: An official handover ceremony with a march, performed by amateurs.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash separates the definition from the wordplay; PRO is removed from the front of the parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A cession is the formal giving up of territory or rights, typically by treaty between states.

clue.text: Common genus of flowers in picture

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: Rosa is the botanical genus of roses

explanation.surface: A widespread type of flower appears in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common genus' reads as one phrase, but 'Common' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means ordinary and unremarkable, lacking poetry or imagination, as commonplace things are.

clue.text: Peer has company — note a lot of misgiving

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A lord keeps company but is full of doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' suggests a member of the House of Lords, but here it means an equal.
explanation.definitionFit: A coequal is someone of the same rank or standing as another, which is what a peer is.

clue.text: Mostly silly about Ecstasy and unwilling to listen

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone high on drugs, acting daft and ignoring all advice.
explanation.walkthrough: DAFT loses its T and wraps around E.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deaf to something is to refuse to heed it, an idiomatic extension of being unable to hear.

clue.text: Honey bear indeed, all empty, and cross

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its insides, leaving only its outermost letters

explanation.surface: A hungry bear finds its honey pots all empty and is very angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the bear's mood, but it is a noun meaning a mixed breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is the offspring of two different species or varieties, which breeders call a cross.

clue.text: Once more get control over historic London bus after missing out

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so those letters are removed from the word

parts.note: the Routemaster is the classic red London double-decker bus

explanation.surface: Regaining command of an old London bus after it had gone off its route.
explanation.walkthrough: The Routemaster ran on London streets from the 1950s to 2005, with an open platform at the back; take OUT from its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To master is to gain control of, so to remaster, in this literal reading, is to take control of it again.

clue.text: Make a channel carrying spring's discharge

indicators.note: to carry something is to bear it within, so one piece holds another

parts.note: to ditch is to dig a channel
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Digging a trench to carry away the outflow from a spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring's discharge' reads as water flowing out, but the 's means 'is': the result is the discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch is to send off or to get rid of, which is what discharging someone or something does.

clue.text: Fabled capital, unknown and fantastically covered in gold

indicators.note: something covered in another is wrapped by it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: done fantastically means in a wild, unreal way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A legendary city of unknown location, fabulously gilded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' is not a link here: its three letters are rearranged and put inside the gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanadu was Kublai Khan's summer capital, made legendary by Coleridge's poem as a place of magnificent splendour.

clue.text: More stern and rising cruelty Cain rates regularly

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Cain, the Bible's first murderer, grades cruelty and grows harsher.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every other letter starting from the second, then read them upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Stricter means more severe in enforcing rules, which is what being sterner amounts to.

clue.text: Given water monster on Tweed, we got away

parts.note: the Hydra was the many-headed water monster killed by Hercules

indicators.note: whatever got away has left, so those letters are no longer there

explanation.surface: A water beast in the River Tweed, and we escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' does double duty in the surface; the Hydra lived in a lake, and the Tweed is a Scottish border river, here just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrated describes something that has absorbed or been supplied with water, as a plant or body is.

clue.text: Self-satisfied group with upsetting intimacy and amorous latitude

indicators.note: upsetting things knocks them over into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smug clique that causes offence with its closeness and freedom in romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' looks like an adjective for the intimacy, but it acts on the three words after it; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutual admiration society is an ironic name for people who praise each other excessively, a complacent little circle.

clue.text: Temporarily suspended — a chance there's no returning in it

indicators.note: something that is in it sits inside the preceding piece

parts.note: a bet is a chance taken

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters run the opposite way

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A plan put on hold, with a slim chance of it ever coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No returning' reads as 'no comeback', but it is an old word for no turned round, and 'in it' puts that inside the preceding wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyant means in abeyance, a state of being temporarily set aside or held in suspense.

clue.text: People who fight OAP protected by son run away finally

indicators.note: whatever is protected is surrounded by its guards, so one piece sits inside others

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
an OAP, old age pensioner, is an oldie
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: finally points to the end of a word, so only its last letter is kept

explanation.surface: Fighters turn up; a pensioner sheltered by his son finally runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP stands for old age pensioner, a British term for a retired person; the pensioner sits between the son and the run-plus-last-letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiery is a collective noun for soldiers, the body of people whose job is fighting.

clue.text: Design a river flat

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An architect designs a riverside apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a noun, an apartment, but it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: Planar describes something lying in a single plane, a geometrical word for level and two-dimensional.

clue.text: Making things easy, exploit perhaps minted ring

parts.note: mint is one herb, so minted is an example of herbed
a ding is the sound of a bell ringing

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of a newly struck coin makes life comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minted' suggests coins or wealth, but here it is food flavoured with mint; 'perhaps' warns it is one example of a wider word.
explanation.definitionFit: Featherbedding means pampering or cushioning people from hardship, like giving them a soft feather mattress.

clue.text: Student teacher? Pity one unfortunately covering nearly everything

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap round it, so one piece surrounds another
things going unfortunately have gone wrong, so the letters fall into a new order
nearly means not quite complete, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: the universe is everything there is

explanation.surface: Someone training to be a teacher, sadly trying to cover the entire syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Student teacher' suggests a trainee; the question mark flags that it is an institution that teaches students. The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: The Open University educates students remotely, so it is quite literally a teacher of students.

clue.text: Totally unconscious justice

explanation.surface: Justice that is entirely blind to what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totally unconscious' reads as one phrase, but the first word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means completely and without reservation, as in winning or refusing outright.

clue.text: Customary notice on the end of the enclosure

parts.note: stock, as in a stock phrase, means customary

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the one kept

explanation.surface: The usual sign hanging at the far end of the paddock.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two 'the's: the second one supplies its last letter, the first is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a barrier of upright stakes forming a fenced area, a kind of defensive pen.

clue.text: Bank installing stronghold backs updated version

indicators.note: to back is to move in reverse, so the letters run the other way
to install something is to put it inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a tier is a bank, as of seats

explanation.surface: A bank adds a vault and supports a new system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, but it is a row, as in a bank of seats; 'backs' reads as supports, but it turns everything round.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrofit is equipment added to an existing machine or building to modernise it.

clue.text: Gambling system somewhat dependent on draws

definitions.text: Gambling system somewhat dependent on draws

parts.words: Gambling system somewhat dependent on draws
parts.note: surface reading: a lottery or raffle, where the draw picks winning tickets
setter's reading: drawn matches, which the classic British coupon rewarded

explanation.walkthrough: The pools are a long-running British bet on weekly match results, and the top prize went to predicting score draws.
explanation.definitionFit: Punters forecast which games in a round of fixtures end level, so the payout hinges on tied results.

clue.text: Action over vote name changer?

explanation.surface: Campaigners take action over a vote to rename something.
explanation.walkthrough: A deed poll is the British legal document used to change one's name; 'over' just places the first word above the second in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing this legal declaration is how people in Britain officially adopt a new surname or forename.

clue.text: Instruction note about US vehicle trail

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a ute is a utility vehicle, a pickup
to lag is to trail behind

explanation.surface: A written instruction about following a trail in an American car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instruction' and 'note' suggest a memo, but the note is a sung scale note wrapped round the vehicle and the trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is teaching or guidance given by a tutor, which amounts to instruction.

clue.text: Rule about dry ice or potassium structure

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round others

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A scientific principle about the crystal shape of dry ice or potassium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry ice' reads as frozen carbon dioxide, but dry is a separate piece meaning teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Latticework is a framework of crossed strips with gaps between them, an interlaced construction.

clue.text: Clue, for instance, is a curse!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a word made of four letters, as the word clue is
second meaning: a swear word, many of which are four letters long

explanation.surface: A frustrated solver exclaims that a crossword clue is a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: The self-referential joke: the word 'Clue' itself is the example, being four letters long.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes any word of four letters and idiomatically means an obscene or offensive swear word.

clue.text: Reportedly what sailors would take to be compass points

indicators.note: a report is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts and the spelling may differ

parts.note: sailors traditionally had a daily ration of rum

explanation.surface: Supposedly, sailors used their drink as a guide to direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy issued sailors a daily tot of rum until 1970.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhumb is one of the thirty-two points of the mariner's compass, and the line of constant bearing.

clue.text: Broadcasting lots then dropping 50 per cent of all material

indicators.note: losing half of every word leaves only its front portion

parts.note: taken as written, then cut to its first six letters
taken as written, then cut to its first two letters
taken as written, then cut to its first two letters

explanation.surface: A station airs plenty of content, then cuts half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Then' looks like a sequence word joining two steps, but it is one of the three words that get halved.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcloth is a fine, densely woven fabric, originally wool, now often cotton for shirts.

clue.text: Prompt is visible to audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the words count by their sound

explanation.surface: A theatre cue or prompt can be seen by the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' suggests a stage prompter, but it is the verb meaning to spur on.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to urge or stir someone into action, which is what prompting them does.

clue.text: As some maps are to deceive, not easy going

explanation.surface: Some maps are meant to mislead, making the journey hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not easy going' reads as rough terrain, but it means not relaxed in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A conformal map projection preserves angles and local shapes, like the Mercator projection used for navigation.

clue.text: How one may receive holiday home which helps one slow down?

indicators.note: one may receive words by ear, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: a pad is slang for a home

explanation.surface: Someone receives a holiday cottage where they can unwind and take it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow down' reads as relaxing on holiday; the question mark flags the literal sense of braking.
explanation.definitionFit: Brake pads press against a car's discs to create friction, reducing the vehicle's speed.

clue.text: Quiet meal, but not opening large cask as before

definitions.note: as before marks the word as old-fashioned

indicators.note: without its opening a word loses its first letter

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A quiet dinner, though the big barrel stays sealed as it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' suggests broaching the cask, but it is the first letter of the meal that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A puncheon is a big barrel of historic size for wine, beer or spirits, a term now largely archaic.

clue.text: Former pope from a wealthy satellite town

parts.note: Urban was the name of eight popes

explanation.surface: An ex-pontiff comes from a rich commuter town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former pope' suggests one who has retired, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Exurban refers to the prosperous areas beyond the suburbs where well-off commuters live.

clue.text: Church service openings can be dull occasions

parts.note: none, or nones, is the church office said at the ninth hour

explanation.surface: The start of a church service can be a boring affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openings' looks like the beginnings of services, but it means holes or outlets.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-event is something anticipated that turns out uneventful and disappointing, an occasion where nothing happens.

clue.text: What one tries to live up to as oldie struggling with age

definitions.text: What one tries to live up to

indicators.note: struggling means thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly person battling with getting older tries to live up to their past.
explanation.walkthrough: The ego ideal is a psychoanalytic term for the inner image of the person one aspires to be.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian theory this is the self-image of perfection that a person measures themselves against.

clue.text: A wonder of old tapestry with areas of flowers round fine little lake on

parts.note: a tapestry is a wall hanging
gardens are areas where flowers grow
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A marvellous antique tapestry showing flower beds around a small lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' reads as a preposition, but it is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon were one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

clue.text: A section of mascarpone pie, certainly not cut

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single slice of the pie
second meaning: made whole, without separate parts, like a swimsuit

explanation.surface: A slice of cheesecake, which surely has not been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads like a hidden word inside the pie; it is a plain description of a slice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a single portion and also describes a garment or object formed as one unbroken whole.

clue.text: The man carries a crash helmet in compound

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: lid is slang for a helmet

explanation.surface: A man brings his motorcycle helmet into a walled yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' suggests an enclosure, but it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A halide is a chemical compound of a halogen such as chlorine with another element, like salt.

clue.text: Shady dealer with small celebrity backing

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: A crooked trader with the support of a minor star.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is British slang for a flashy petty crook, typically selling black-market goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a small-time swindler trading in dubious goods, the very type of a shady dealer.

clue.text: Military insignia university prohibited

parts.note: a tab is a coloured collar badge on a staff officer's uniform
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Army badges are banned at the university.
explanation.walkthrough: TABU is a variant spelling of taboo.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tabu is forbidden by custom or religion, so it is banned from use or mention.

clue.text: Plant with corm — not a root shows

indicators.note: what shows is on display, so the letters sit plainly in the clue text

explanation.surface: A botanical note: this plant has a corm, which is not a root.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes a true botanical point, since a corm is a swollen stem rather than a root.
explanation.definitionFit: Taro is a tropical plant grown for its starchy underground corm, eaten cooked in many cuisines.

clue.text: Religious leader hit hard over article

explanation.surface: A cleric is hit hard over a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper story, but it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a spiritual teacher in Tibetan Buddhism, like the Dalai Lama.

clue.text: Opening of second of songs Mahler's rewritten

indicators.note: rewritten text is put down again differently, so the letters are rearranged
the second of a word is its second letter, which is the one kept

explanation.surface: The start of the second of Mahler's song cycles has been revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening of second' looks like one phrase, but 'Opening' is the definition and the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An armhole is the gap in a garment through which the arm passes, a hole in the fabric.

clue.text: One may want spread here, having a spell of good luck

definitions.meaning: first meaning: where butter goes, on a bread roll

definitions.text: having a spell of good luck
definitions.meaning: second meaning: enjoying a run of success

explanation.surface: Someone wants their good fortune to spread while it lasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' suggests something extending, but it is butter or jam.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a streak of successes, and literally the place where butter is put on bread.

clue.text: Regularly clued-up and ready in Europe

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A European who is well informed and always prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' reads as prepared, but it is British slang for cash; the leu is Romania's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The leu is the monetary unit of Romania and Moldova, so it is cash in part of Europe.

clue.text: American I had over one August night for starters

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the letters run backwards
starters are the first things, so only initial letters are kept

explanation.surface: A US visitor recalls a summer night when he had a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I had' tempts you toward I'D, but only 'had' is turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: An Idahoan is a native or resident of Idaho, a state in the north-western United States.

clue.text: Improbability of oiled hunk cooking with oil?

indicators.note: cooking mixes and transforms ingredients, so the letters are combined anew

explanation.surface: How unlikely is it that a greased-up muscleman would be frying with oil?
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'oil' is not repetition: its letters join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlikelihood is the state of being improbable, a less common synonym for unlikeliness.

clue.text: Dynasty left fools — they lower the level of brightness

definitions.text: they lower the level of brightness

parts.note: the Sung or Song dynasty ruled China from 960 to 1279
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A ruling family left behind idiots who dim the brightest minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower the level of brightness' suggests making people less clever, but it means cutting glare.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinted spectacles reduce the intensity of daylight reaching the eyes, cutting glare from the sun.
